Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception

Class QueryException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception.DatabaseException
org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception.QueryException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
Direct Known Subclasses:
ForeignKeyViolationException, UniqueConstraintViolationException
public class QueryException extends DatabaseException
Reports a statement the database refused, with the connection name, SQL and bindings.

The message is SQL: <sql> (Connection: <name>, SQL state <state>, vendor code <code>), where the state is unknown when the database gave none. The binding values and the database's own error text (Reason: ...) are appended only when the connection was built with showBindingsInErrors(true), because both can hold personal data; getBindings() carries the values either way. In the message, the SQL, the reason, the connection name, the SQL state and the values are escaped: a backslash is doubled, line breaks appear as \r and \n, and other control characters and Unicode line separators as \uXXXX. The SQL and the reason are cut after 1000 code points and the name, the SQL state and each value after 256 (all marked with ...), and a byte[] value appears as <n bytes>.

With the default settings the database's own error text is kept only in the cause, because databases often echo the offending values in it. A log line or report that prints the whole cause chain shows that text whatever the settings, so send only Throwable.getMessage() to places that must not see personal data.

The serialized form leaves out the binding values when they were hidden from the message, and after deserialization getBindings() is then empty. Only the bindings field is left out: the cause (the driver failure, which may hold the database's own error text) and any suppressed exceptions are serialized as usual.

Instances are immutable after construction and safe to share between threads.

      public QueryException(String connectionName, String sql, List<?> bindings, DriverException cause, boolean showBindings)
      Creates a query failure from the driver failure that caused it.
      Parameters:
      connectionName - the name of the connection, never null
      sql - the statement that failed, never null
      bindings - the binding values, never null, elements may be null; the list is copied
      cause - the driver failure, never null
      showBindings - whether the binding values are appended to the message
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if any reference argument is null
